gradation

/gray-DAY-shun/ - three beats, stress on DAY · noun

Hear It

What It Means

A gradation is one step in a gradual, ordered series — a slight, orderly shift in shade, degree, or stage between one level and the next.

The paint store's sample wall held forty gradations of white, and Nadia could no longer tell where 'ivory' surrendered to 'bone.'

Example

The luthier's sandpaper rack ran from 80-grit to 2000, and the apprentice's first month went to learning its gradations — which step erases the scratches the last one left, and why skipping two steps costs an afternoon.

Gradation is the word for each of those orderly steps on a scale, and for the step-by-step climb they make together. The change comes by degrees, every level defined by its neighbors above and below. Where difference blends smoothly with no steps at all, shading is the better word; where it jumps all at once, a leap; the gradation lives between them — difference taken one step at a time.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

shading: Shading is the painter's word for continuous, blended change — one tone melting into the next with no steps at all. A gradation keeps its steps: you can point to where one level ends and the next begins.

increment: An increment is a measured, usually equal addition — the thermostat's two degrees, the annual raise. A gradation may be too subtle to measure at all; what it promises is not a fixed amount but a scale that moves by degrees.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

leap: an abrupt jump that skips the steps between

uniformity: one unvarying shade or level throughout

Where it sits · how boldly the difference between neighbors shows

nuance → gradation → contrast

nuance vs. gradation: A nuance is fainter than a gradation — a difference so slight that most eyes miss it entirely, while a gradation is a step you can point to on the scale.

contrast vs. gradation: A contrast is stronger than a gradation: a gradation eases from one level to the next by a visible step, while a contrast sets two levels boldly against each other, plain at a glance.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — grad: a step (Latin gradus)

Suffix — -ation: the act or result of

Put it together: Grad- (a step) + -ation (the result of) = a stepping — the scale a series of steps builds, or any one stair within it. Latin gradus is one of English's busiest roots, hiding in words for ranks, slopes, ceremonies, and every kind of stepwise motion; gradation is the family's quietest member, the step itself.

Use the root in a new word: gradient: The surveyor's notebook recorded the gradient of every lane in the county, and she could quote the three worst from memory.

Root Check

Word Choice

precise / descriptive

Gradation is for scales: color charts, registers of politeness, degrees of severity. Two neighbors to keep straight — a spectrum is the whole range laid end to end, while a gradation is one step within it; and a grade is the rank assigned, while a gradation is the interval a scale climbs by. If the change happens all at once, the word you want is leap or break, not gradation.
